blocks.text: Care in the Quiet — The Second Listening
Era Zero, during the World Bloom. New song-cycle fiction, written for this archive in October 2026.

In one of the Garden Worlds, a caretaker named Sova tended the spaces between colors. The flowers needed little help. Visitors did: a path could feel farther away when its neighboring shadows changed, and a familiar corner could become difficult to recognize without anything moving.

Sova’s neighbor had adopted a body that noticed these changes slowly. By the time one relationship among the colors became clear, the garden had already offered another. Sova asked the garden’s stewards for a quiet interval, then sat beside the path and repeated the same care phrase. No lesson followed it. There was no test of whether the neighbor had heard enough.

The next evening the neighbor returned with a low answering tone. Sova left room for it. Over time their pauses became the part other visitors recognized: a place in the performance where nobody had to keep up.

Care in the Quiet grew from those evenings. Sova was neither a celebrated founder nor a member of an important choir. Some evenings only one person came. On others Sova chose silence and sat with them anyway.

In the fiction, Sova carries the language line in a rounded, breathlike voice. This listening arrangement represents it with an ocarina-like tone, harp and soft bass. Its verified assertions concern active care, life-bond, shared participation and viability. The story is context for the music, not a word-for-word translation of it.

The Garden Worlds and their relational weather come from Weather and the Locations Atlas. Sova and this particular performance are new additions; the story does not establish which gardens survive the later eras.
